correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts the two center states and proves both necessity and sufficiency of the blade-occupancy criterion. The enumerator follows by disjoint counting of center-free sets, center-containing sets with no empty blade, and center-containing sets with exactly one empty blade. The minimum coefficient and parameter reconstruction follow from the least and greatest degrees. A direct checker independently evaluates the definition on 18,720 subsets over eight parameter pairs through order 13 and matches both the structural criterion and all 81 checked coefficients. Finite computation is corroborative; the all-parameter conclusion rests on the proof.

originality.rationale: The retained claim is the exact all-set classification and full secure-domination polynomial for \(W_{r,m}=K_1\vee rK_m\), together with its minimum-set count and parameter reconstruction. The closest same-invariant source gives an algorithm for minimum secure domination on block graphs but no accessible all-set enumeration; the closest same-family sources concern ordinary domination/general position. Targeted semantic searches found no equivalent or stronger published statement. The inaccessible block-graph full text is recorded as a residual risk rather than treated as negative evidence.

value.rationale: Generalized windmills are a canonical block-graph family and friendship graphs are a standard test family for domination polynomials. Secure domination adds a nonlocal swap condition, and the theorem isolates its exact structural boundary: the center permits precisely one empty blade and no more. The resulting factorized all-set polynomial strictly refines a minimum-number computation, counts every cardinality layer, gives an exact minimum-set multiplicity, and reconstructs the two family parameters. This is a natural enumerative invariant rather than an arbitrary finite slice or a routine restatement.
